title: Have you thought of the verb 'have'...

topics.name: 'Have' as a main verb (possession, relations, events, meals, illness)
Negatives and questions with do + have

questions.rule: Our school is a singular subject, so the main verb is has.
Use do with you, and after do/does always use the base form have.

options: Kabir has a bad cold this week.
Kabir is having a bad cold this week.
Kabir is have a bad cold this week.
questions.rule: For an illness, have is used in the simple form: has a cold, not is having a cold.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct verb form.
options: They have come back from Pune.
They have came back from Pune.
They has come back from Pune.
questions.rule: The present perfect is have/has + past participle: have come.

options: My grandparents did not had a television in 1970.
My grandparents does not have a television in 1970.
My grandparents did not have a television in 1970.
questions.rule: The past negative of main verb have is did not have; after did, use the base form.

options: Mrs Rao has her car repaired yesterday.
Mrs Rao had her car repair yesterday.
Mrs Rao had her car repaired yesterday.
questions.rule: Causative: had + object + past participle. Yesterday needs the past: had her car repaired.

options: My friend and her sister have a pet parrot.
My friend and her sister has a pet parrot.
My friend and her sister having a pet parrot.
questions.rule: Two subjects joined by and are plural, so use have.

options: Meena is having this phone since 2022.
Meena has had this phone since 2022.
questions.rule: With since, use the present perfect. Main verb have + perfect gives has had.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Neha is third person singular, so use has.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: With a singular subject like Rohan, the negative is doesn't have.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After has in a perfect tense, use the past participle: has written.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Someone else did the work: have + object + past participle - had our house painted.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After let us, use the base form of the verb: let us have a party.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The subject is one (of my cousins), which is singular, so use has.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Use for with a length of time (ten years) and since with a starting point (2015).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Every one is singular, so the helping verb is has: has had a check-up.
Last year is in the past, so use had.

questions.after: you have a spare pen, Kunal?
questions.rule: Questions with main verb have use do/does. With you, use Do.
For a daily habit with we, use the simple present have.
Present perfect with a plural subject: have arrived.

questions.before: Dad is going to have the leaking tap
questions.rule: A plumber will do it: have + object + past participle - have the tap fixed.

questions.before: Sara doesn't have a cold today,
questions.rule: The sentence uses doesn't, so the tag uses the positive does: does she?

questions.before: By the time the doctor arrived, the patient
questions.rule: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect: had taken.
Get + object + past participle means someone else did it: got her tyre mended.
Use have for a physical condition: I have a headache.
Question with main verb have: Does + subject + have.

questions.prompt: Say that a painter is doing the work.
questions.rule: Get + object + past participle: getting our kitchen painted.
How long asks about a period up to now, so use the present perfect: have you had.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a reason.
questions.rule: Past negative of main verb have: didn't have; because gives the reason.

chat: Do you have a pencil, Tara?
questions.rule: With I, the main verb is have.

chat: What would you like to have, tea or coffee?
questions.rule: After will ('ll), use the base form: I'll have.

chat: Why were you absent yesterday, Pooja?
options: I have had a high fever yesterday, ma'am.
I has a high fever, ma'am.
I had a high fever, ma'am.
questions.rule: The illness was in the past (yesterday), so use the simple past had.

chat: Have you seen the new Marathi film yet?
options: No, I didn't saw it yet.
No, I haven't seen it yet.
No, I haven't saw it yet.
questions.rule: Present perfect negative: haven't + past participle - haven't seen.

options: Yes, I had it cut yesterday.
Yes, I had it cutting yesterday.
Yes, I have it cut yesterday.
questions.rule: The barber did it in the past: had + it + past participle - had it cut.

chat: You don't have school tomorrow, do you?
options: No, I don't. It's a holiday.
No, I doesn't. It's a holiday.
No, I not. It's a holiday.
questions.rule: A short answer repeats the helping verb: No, I don't.

chat: Did you have a good time at the wedding?
I heard there was a band.
options: Yes, I did! The band played till midnight.
Yes, I had! The band played till midnight.
Yes, I did! The band was played till midnight.
questions.rule: The question uses did, so the short answer is I did; the band itself played (active).

chat: Has Dev recovered from his cold?
options: Not yet. He is having it since Monday.
Not yet. He has it since Monday.
Not yet. He has had it since Monday.
questions.rule: A state from Monday till now takes the present perfect: has had.
Negative of main verb have: doesn't have (base form after does).

options: Does your brother has a laptop?
Does your brother have a laptop?
Do your brother have a laptop?
questions.rule: Use Does with a singular subject, then the base form have.

questions.prompt: Change into the present perfect tense.
questions.source: Smita wrote a letter to her grandmother.
options: Smita has wrote a letter to her grandmother.
Smita has written a letter to her grandmother.
Smita have written a letter to her grandmother.
questions.rule: Present perfect: has + past participle - has written.

questions.source: The tailor stitched my school uniform.
options: I had my school uniform stitch by the tailor.
I had my school uniform stitching by the tailor.
I had my school uniform stitched by the tailor.
questions.rule: Causative: had + object + past participle - had my uniform stitched.

options: Ravi said that he had a headache.
Ravi said that I had a headache.
Ravi said that he has had a headache.
questions.rule: After said, I have becomes he had: change the pronoun and move the tense back.

options: Sanika doesn't have any brothers, doesn't she?
Sanika doesn't have any brothers, does she?
Sanika doesn't have any brothers, has she?
questions.rule: A negative sentence with doesn't takes a positive tag: does she?

questions.source: The workers have repaired the old bridge.
options: The old bridge has repaired by the workers.
The old bridge has been repaired by the workers.
The old bridge have been repaired by the workers.
questions.rule: Present perfect passive: has/have been + past participle; bridge is singular - has been.

questions.source: As soon as we had our dinner, the power went off.
options: No sooner had we had our dinner than the power went off.
No sooner we had our dinner than the power went off.
No sooner had we had our dinner when the power went off.
questions.rule: No sooner takes inverted order (had we) and pairs with than, not when.
